newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Vote in Mauritian capital postponed after killings.
newsitem.headline: Vote in Mauritian capital postponed after killings.

text.p: Municipal voting in three of the six wards in the Mauritian capital, Port Louis, was postponed on Sunday after two men were killed, the electoral supervisory commission said.
Police sources said Zulficar Bheeky, 38, and Abdal Joomun, 33, died in the Plaine Verte suburb, after being shot by eight masked men travelling in a stolen van.
A third man, Yousouf Moorat was in critical condition with a head wound. Two other men were also taken to hospital with slight injuries.

Voting in Plaine Verte and the two adjoining wards was postponed until November 17. Voting in the three remaining wards of Port Louis and in four other Mauritian towns went ahead as scheduled on Sunday.
Bheeky and Joomun were activists for political parties contesting the municipal elections, and the shootings were seen as politically motivated.
"This was a cold-blooded crime," Deputy Prime Minister Paul Berenger told reporters. Echoing calls from political parties taking part in the elections, President Cassam Uteem called for calm.
